result.shared_observations: All options must address the specific needs of the kayak patrol while navigating the constraints of technology and user preferences.

result.system_overview: The target system operates within a coastal town where a volunteer kayak patrol requires a distress signaling mechanism for kayakers who are out for 2-3 hours. The current system relies on a group text that is often ignored, indicating a need for a more reliable and passive distress signal. The system must function with limited cellular signal and respect user privacy by avoiding constant GPS tracking. The options under consideration aim to provide a lightweight check-in/check-out system that can signal distress without active engagement from the user.

Reinforcing.Description: Increased usage of the distress signaling method leads to higher awareness and responsiveness among patrol members.
Assumptions: Users will adopt the new system if it is perceived as reliable
Increased awareness will lead to quicker responses to distress signals

Balancing.Description: The need for privacy may limit the effectiveness of distress signaling methods that require constant tracking.
Assumptions: Users prioritize privacy over constant monitoring
Privacy concerns will limit the adoption of certain technologies

bottlenecks.description: Limited cellular signal may hinder the effectiveness of all proposed options.
